abstract: Human placental lactogen (HPL or HCS), the beta subunit of human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-HCG), and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) were measured by a specific radioimmunoassay in plasma of 65 patients with ovarian cancer. Fifty-one patients had epithelial tumors, while 14 had germ cell tumors. It was found that 47 patients (72 per cent) had high levels of plasma HPL, 29 patients (45 per cent) had high levels of plasma beta-HCG, and 34 patients (52 per cent) had high levels of plasma CEA, but there was no correlation between these protein marker levels in different patients. Twenty of these patients were studied before and after operation and during chemotherapy and/or radiotherpy. There was no consistent correlation between these marker levels and the course of the disease. These data suggest that measurement of HPL, beta-HCG, and CEA in sera of patients with ovarian cancer is not of value in assessing the clinical status of the patients or in determining the effect of therapy.
abstract_ja: 卵巣癌患者65例の血漿中で、ヒト胎盤性ラクトゲン（HPLまたはHCS）、ヒト絨毛性ゴナドトロピン(hCG)のβサブユニット（β-hCG）、およびCEA（癌胎児性抗原）を特異的放射免疫測定法で測定した。上皮性腫瘍が51例、胚細胞腫瘍が14例であった。47例（72％）で血漿HPLが高値、29例（45％）で血漿β-hCGが高値、34例（52％）でCEAが高値であったが、異なる患者間でこれらのタンパク質マーカー値に相関は認められなかった。このうち20例は、手術前後および化学療法や放射線療法の期間中に検討された。これらのマーカー値と疾患経過との間に一貫した相関は認められなかった。これらのデータは、卵巣癌患者の血清中のHPL、β-hCG、CEAの測定は、患者の臨床状態の評価や治療効果の判定には価値がないことを示唆している。
